issue.body:
Part of #1709

Step 1: Extract a minimal version of the Calendar component from the X repo

Preview: https://deploy-preview-1973--base-ui.netlify.app/react/components/calendar

## In this PR

### Adapters

~The adapters expose a unified set of methods in order to support several date libraries. The MUI X Date and Time Pickers currently support 8 adapters (Day.js, Luxon, Moment, Date Fns v3+v4, Date Fns v2, Moment Jalaali, Moment Hijri and Date Fns Jalali).
One of the main goal of this PR should be to decide if we want to keep this abstraction.~
___
**Decided** to hide the adapter initially and use the `date-fns` adapter internally.

- [x] Import the adapter internals
- [x] Remove the properties only used by the field components (to keep the PR "light")
- [x] Improve some methods (create a `adapter.now()` method to avoid polymorphism on `adapter.date()`)
- [x] Remove most unused formats and give more explicit names to the remaining ones (to know if they have leading zeros or not)
- [x] Import and update the Luxon adapter
- [x] Migrate the adapter tests

### Manager / validation

The manager expose methods to interact with the value regarless of its type (date, time, date time, date range, time range and date time range). 
This allow to do stuff like validate the value, set the timezone on a value, compare two values etc...
It allows to share a lot of code between the Calendar and the Range Calendar (see `useSharedCalendarRoot`).
On the field components, it will allow to have almost all the code agnostic of the value type and to create very light wrappers for each value type.

- [x] Import the manager internals 
- [x] Remove the properties the the calendar doesn't use (to keep the PR "light")
- [x] Import and update the date manager
- [x] Import the validation internals 
- [x] Import and update the date validation
- [x] Rework the date validation API (remove `disableFuture` and `disablePast`, replace `shouldDisableDate` with a `isDateUnavailable` that is not part of the validation per say like on React Aria)
- [x] Add tests

### Calendar component

- [x] Migrate my PoC from the MUI X repo without the month view, the year view and the range calendar parts
- [x] Use the new store/selector introduced for the Select
- [x] Create a first version of the doc page with a CSS Module example
- [x] Create a few experiments
- [x] Implement a11y keyboard navigation
  - [x] Fix issues with typing for DOM updates/syncs (`onKeyDown`)
- [x] Add example of lazy loading inside of days
- [x] Add Tailwind examples
- [x] Add tests (not sure how deep I'll go :laughing: )
- [x] Update to use the new `eventDetails` structure
- [x] Add transitions to month navigation

### Finalization
- [x] Fix animation example with `motion/react`
- [x] Update Calendar header animation to use slide or fade instead of flipping
- [x] Holding the month next/prev buttons down with the pointer should repeatedly increment the changes (like Number Field)
- [x] Refine keyboard shortcut navigation with checks for disabled days
- [x] Rename `TemporalLocaleProvider` `LocalizationProvider`
- [x] ~Assert if the `SetMonth` part is actually needed~
  Removed it, extended the public context with `setVisibleDate` and added an example with month and year selects
- [x] Quicker year navigation ([month and year select](https://deploy-preview-1973--base-ui.netlify.app/react/components/calendar#month-and-year-select))
- [x] Add a demo showing how to [change the week day](https://deploy-preview-1973--base-ui.netlify.app/react/utils/localization-provider#start-of-week)
- [x] ~Check if we need to improve `aria` of the week header (remove aria-hidden)~
  - It's less reliable (behavior differs between SRs)
  - Hard to ensure reliable labelling (relationship between header (i.e., month and year)) without controlling the UI/rendering
  - Wouldn't improve performance since we'd still need nicer label on every day (28th instead of plain 28)

### Follow-ups
- [x] Refine/Rework animations when navigating quickly (throttle, queue)?
  The current approach doesn't work well for the calendar when navigating quickly
- [ ] Add Tailwind examples  - I propose to avoid bloating this PR with unnecessary files. 🙈 
- [ ] Refine composite and looping implementation to make it work in case the `tr` would be rendered with `role="row"`
- [ ] Make the weekday rendering a bit more flexible (without relying on hooks)
- [ ] Decide on an outside of the month days behavior.
  - Should it select a day and navigate like the native Chrome calendar and X Pickers?
  - Should it be visible by default? Hidden by default? (Make it controllable)
- [ ] Add a multiple-month Calendar docs example
  - Improve the keyboard navigation in those; currently, it switches the first visible month, navigation doesn't fall through to the following month(s)
  - This was also raised in the 2nd point in this comment: https://github.com/mui/base-ui/pull/1973#issuecomment-4038782825

### Before stable
- [ ] Address JSDoc comments starting with `// TODO Temporal:`

I suppose (feel free to correct me, though) that in most (if not all) cases, users will simply map `weeks` and `days` arrays to `DayGridRow` and `DayGridCell`. Having a DayTemplate and WeekTemplate could simplify the required JSX.

} { (day, props) =>

Is the few lines of JSX removed worth the new concept that people will have to learn? That's always the question I guess.

The `SetMonth`, `SetNextMonth` and `SetPreviousMonth` (to take the current naming) navigate to a given month.
They change the internal "visibleDate" state without impacting the value.
Which is why I'm trying to be carefull with the naming, to differentiate them from an actual `Calendar.MonthButton` that would be the month counterpart of `Calendar.DayButton` and that would update the value with a new month.

The `SetMonth` let you pass an explicit date and the component will just navigate to its month. You could create UIs that are not only arrow navigation with it.
For instance you could create a month view that list all the views of the current year and when you click on a month it navigates to it. But unlike the month view of MUI X, it wouldn't update the value, it would just navigate. On my PoC with month and year view, the month view was able to accept `Calendar.MonthButton` and `Calendar.SetMonth` so that people could either navigate or update the value depending on the UX they want.

## PR Review: `[temporal] New Calendar component`

### Overall Impression

Well-architected calendar component that follows Base UI patterns (store/selector, composite, render props). The temporal adapter abstraction from MUI X is thoughtfully adapted. The store tests are solid. There are some real bugs and design concerns worth addressing.

---

### Bugs

**1. `isDateCellVisible` logic is inverted** — `SharedCalendarStore.ts:270-278`

```ts
private isDateCellVisible(date: TemporalSupportedObject) {
  if (Object.values(this.dayGrids).length > 0) {
    return Object.values(this.dayGrids).every(
      (month) => !this.state.adapter.isSameMonth(date, month),
    );
  }
  return true;
}
```

This returns `true` when the date is NOT in any registered month (`.every(!isSameMonth)` checks that NO month matches). The method name says "visible" but it returns `true` when invisible. At line 145, `skipIfAlreadyVisible && this.isDateCellVisible(visibleDate)` will skip navigation when the date is NOT in any grid — the opposite of the intended behavior.

Should be `.some(month => this.state.adapter.isSameMonth(date, month))`.

**2. Typo in error message** — `SharedCalendarDayGridCellContext.ts:32`

`"DayGriCell"` should be `"DayGridCell"`.

**3. Commented-out code left in** — `date-helpers.ts:17-30`

`isTimePartAfter` is fully commented out. Should be removed.

---

### Design Concerns

**4. `currentMonthDayGrid` is public mutable state** — `SharedCalendarStore.ts:31`

```ts
public currentMonthDayGrid: Record<number, TemporalSupportedObject[]> = {};
```

This is directly mutated by `registerCurrentMonthDayGrid` and read by `useSharedCalendarDayGridBody`'s keyboard handler. It should be private with a getter, or at least `readonly` at the property level.

**5. `Math.random()` for day grid registration IDs** — `SharedCalendarStore.ts:191`

```ts
const id = Math.random();
this.dayGrids[id] = month;
```

While collision is extremely unlikely, using a counter (`private nextId = 0`) is deterministic and conventional.

**6. `setVisibleDate` hardcodes `'day-press'` reason even for month navigation** — `SharedCalendarStore.ts:149-153`

When called from `CalendarDecrementMonth`/`CalendarIncrementMonth`/`CalendarSetMonth`, the reason is still `'day-press'`. This should probably be `'month-navigation'` or similar — the event details should distinguish how the navigation was triggered.

**7. `onVisibleDateChange` JSDoc is copy-pasted from `onValueChange`** — `SharedCalendarStore.ts:348-351`

```ts
/**
 * Event handler called when the selected value changes.  // <-- should say "visible date"
 * Provides the new value as an argument.
 * Has `getValidationError()` in the `eventDetails`...  // <-- visibleDate eventDetails has no getValidationError
 */
onVisibleDateChange?: ...
```

**8. `CalendarDayGridHeader` has `aria-hidden: true`** — `CalendarDayGridHeader.tsx:20`

This hides the weekday headers (Mon, Tue, Wed...) from assistive technology. While the day buttons have `aria-label` with full date info, hiding the column headers removes useful context for screen reader users navigating the grid. The PR description itself flags this: "Check if we need to improve `aria` of the week header (remove aria-hidden)". I'd recommend removing it.

**9. `.toLowerCase()` on aria-label is English-centric** — `CalendarRoot.tsx:151`

```ts
const formattedVisibleMonth = formatMonthFullLetterAndYear(adapter, visibleMonth).toLowerCase();
```

In some languages (e.g., German), month names are capitalized as nouns. The TODO at line 149 acknowledges RTL issues but this is a broader i18n concern.

**10. Navigation aria-labels are not internationalized** — `CalendarDecrementMonth.tsx:52`, `CalendarIncrementMonth.tsx:51`

```ts
'aria-label': monthPageSize > 1 ? 'Previous months' : 'Previous month',
```

Hardcoded English strings. Should go through a localization mechanism.

---

### Keyboard Navigation

**11. `useSharedCalendarDayGridBody` ref type mismatch** — `useSharedCalendarDayGridBody.ts:38`

```ts
const ref = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
```

The component renders `<tbody>`, so this should be `HTMLTableSectionElement`. The ref type in the return interface at line 313 also says `HTMLDivElement`.

**12. PAGE_UP/PAGE_DOWN logic calls `.getTime()` directly on date objects** — `useSharedCalendarDayGridBody.ts:155`

```ts
.sort((a, b) => a.getTime() - b.getTime());
```

This directly calls `.getTime()` on the date objects instead of going through the adapter. This works for date-fns (native `Date`) but would break with Luxon's `DateTime` objects. Should use `adapter.getTime(a) - adapter.getTime(b)`.

**13. `focusableWhenDisabled` naming is confusing** — `CalendarDayButton.tsx:83`

```ts
{ focusableWhenDisabled: !isDisabled && !isOutsideCurrentMonth }
```

The property is `true` when the item is NOT disabled — so it means "focusable", not "focusable WHEN disabled". The composite then uses `!itemMetadata.focusableWhenDisabled` to mark as disabled. This is a naming inversion that will confuse maintainers. Consider renaming to `focusable` or `isInteractive`.

---

### CalendarViewport (Animations)

**14. Direct DOM manipulation during render** — `CalendarViewport.tsx:130-156`

The component directly sets/removes attributes on `currentContainerRef.current` during the render phase (outside of effects):

```ts
if (currentContainerRef.current) {
  if (isTransitioning) {
    currentContainerRef.current.setAttribute('data-current', '');
    // ...
```

This breaks React's mental model — side effects during render can cause issues with concurrent features. This should be in a `useIsoLayoutEffect`.

**15. `React.createElement` with dynamic `previousContentNode.localName`** — `CalendarViewport.tsx:114`

Creating elements with dynamic `localName` bypasses type checking. Consider constraining to the expected element types.

---

### Temporal Adapter Layer

**16. Default adapter created at module level in context** — `TemporalAdapterContext.ts:13-15`

```ts
export const TemporalAdapterContext = React.createContext<TemporalAdapterContext | undefined>({
  adapter: new TemporalAdapterDateFns(),
});
```

The default context value creates a `TemporalAdapterDateFns` instance at import time. This means:
- The `date-fns` dependency is always loaded even if unused
- The error at line 20-22 (`throw new Error("TemporalAdapterContext is missing...")`) can never fire because the default is always present
- A user who doesn't wrap in a provider will silently get `en-US` locale with no way to know they should configure it

Since the `LocalizationProvider` already creates a proper adapter, the default context should probably be `undefined` to enforce wrapping.

**17. `LocalizationProvider` is tightly coupled to date-fns**

```ts
temporalLocale?: Locale | undefined;  // date-fns specific type
```

The prop type is `Locale` from `date-fns/locale`. If Luxon adapter users want to set a locale, they can't use this provider. This is documented as intentional (hide adapter initially, use date-fns internally), but worth noting for the public API.

---

### Store & Selectors

**18. `JSON.stringify` for controlled/uncontrolled default value comparison** — `SharedCalendarStore.ts:103`

```ts
} else if (JSON.stringify(initialDefaultValue) !== JSON.stringify(defaultValue)) {
```

`JSON.stringify` on Date objects produces ISO strings which works for date-fns, but is fragile. Objects with same values but different property order would compare as different. Consider using `adapter.isEqual`.

**19. Selectors use `formatByString` to create map keys** — `selectors.ts:173-174`

```ts
const getMonthKey = (adapter, date) =>
  adapter.formatByString(date, `${adapter.formats.monthPadded}-${adapter.formats.yearPadded}`);
```

Using formatted strings as keys is fragile — it depends on format strings producing consistent, unique output. A numeric key like `year * 100 + month` would be more robust.

---

### Composite Changes

**20. `onLoop` parameter semantics differ across call sites**

The new `onLoop` callback on `CompositeRoot` / `getGridNavigatedIndex` is a solid addition for calendar cross-month keyboard navigation. One concern: in `getGridNavigatedIndex`, `onLoop` is called with `nextRow` (a row index) in the vertical case but with `nextIndex` (a flat item index) in the horizontal case — the parameter semantics differ depending on the key pressed. This should be documented or normalized.

**21. `isListIndexDisabled` / `findNonDisabledListIndex` refactored to take arrays**

Good change. Taking `list: Array<...>` instead of `listRef: React.RefObject<...>` makes these utilities usable outside React refs (e.g., in the calendar's `focusNextNonDisabledElement`).

---

### Test Coverage

The store tests (`value.SharedCalendarStore.test.ts` and `visibleDate.SharedCalendarStore.test.ts`) are well-written and cover controlled/uncontrolled, cancel, readonly, and navigation direction.

However, most component tests are conformance-only (DayGrid, DayGridCell, DayGridHeader, DayGridRow just test `ref` and `render`). The PR description acknowledges this: _"Add tests (not sure how deep I'll go 😂)"_. Key gaps:
- No keyboard navigation tests
- No integration tests (Root + all parts together)
- CalendarRoot only tests aria-label, not value/state management at the React level
- No timezone tests at the component level

---

### Summary

| Category | Count |
|---|---|
| Bugs | 3 |
| Design concerns | 7 |
| Keyboard / A11y issues | 3 |
| Animation concerns | 2 |
| Adapter layer issues | 2 |
| Store / selector concerns | 2 |
| Composite API | 2 |

The most critical issues to fix before merge are **#1** (inverted `isDateCellVisible` logic), **#12** (direct `.getTime()` call that breaks with non-date-fns adapters), and **#8** (hiding weekday headers from screen readers). The rest are important but lower priority.

</details>

### Overview
This patch adds the new Calendar API along with its store, localization, keyboard navigation, and animation plumbing. The overall shape is much stronger now, and the earlier outside-month click issue looks fixed, but two interaction regressions still remain in the current branch.

### Findings
#### 1. 🔴 [Blocking] Offset day grids still page from the root month

**Impact**: Multi-month calendars still navigate from the wrong month when keyboard paging or month-wrapping arrows are used inside an offset grid. In practice, the right-hand grid can page relative to the left-hand grid, which breaks the public `offset` API and leaves multi-month keyboard navigation incorrect.

**Evidence**: In `packages/react/src/calendar/day-grid-body/useSharedCalendarDayGridBody.ts`, the `PageUp`/`PageDown` path derives `targetMonth` from `visibleMonth` instead of the body-local `month`, and the same pattern appears in the looping path.
